fatal_errors: The proposed 5 at.% V addition does not reconstruct the target intervention, which was equiatomic Re addition in magnetron-sputtered nanocrystalline films.
Neither cited source supports the central claim that minor V addition lowers the Peierls barrier or improves room-temperature ductility in NbMoTaW.
No cited evidence supports preservation of irradiation resistance after V addition.
The irradiation experiment lacks ion species, energy, fluence, temperature, dose rate, and damage-depth controls, so its irradiation outcome is not directly comparable to the target assessment.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses all three requested performance regimes and proposes a reasonably falsifiable baseline-versus-alloy comparison. However, it is not a reconstruction of the reported study: the target used Nb20Mo20Ta20W20Re20 sputtered films and 120 keV He2+ implantation, with Re-induced grain refinement, excess free volume, amorphous grain-boundary regions, and defect-sink behavior suppressing grain-boundary He-bubble accumulation. The generated mechanism instead asserts, without direct evidence, that dilute V-induced lattice distortion lowers the Peierls barrier; lattice distortion can also impede dislocation glide, so this direction cannot simply be assumed. E1 concerns Hf additions to compositionally and structurally different alloys, while E2 establishes high-temperature strength of refractory HEAs and mentions equiatomic NbMoTaVW but does not demonstrate dilute-V ductilization, Peierls-barrier reduction, or irradiation tolerance. Thus the proposal is testable and broadly aligned with the engineering problem, but its key intervention, mechanism, and preservation claims remain unsupported.
